issuer: the Illinois Secretary of State, Driver Services
note: The Secretary of State's basic fees page (read 2026-10-30) gives a driver's licence, ages 21 to 68, at $30 (ages 18 to 20, $5) and a five-year state ID card, ages 18 to 64, at $20; the FAQ says a licence is valid for 4 years and an ID card for 5. The $30 licence is kept from 21, the youngest age it is issued at (a driver under 21 is under the graduated licence programme, the licence page says; the $5 licence of 18 to 20 isn't held). No youngest age for the card was read (cards are sold under 18). On 2026-10-30 the file was rewritten with the terms set by the holder's age, from the same fee page and the licence and ID page: the licence for 4 years at $30 from 21 to 68, $5 from 69 to 80 and $2 from 81 to 86, and for 1 year, free, from 87 (the page has drivers of 87 and older renew each year); the card for 5 years at $5 under 18 and $20 from 18 to 64, and free and non-expiring from 65 (the fee page says 65 or older, the ID page 'over age 65'; 65 is held, a reading). Until then the file held the licence of 21 to 68 (4 years, $30) and the card of 18 to 64 (5 years, $20) only.

Driver's License – Persons ages 81 to 86 $2 ... Driver's License – Persons age 87 and older Free ... State ID Card – Five-year, under age 18 $5 ... State ID Card – Persons 65 or older Free

sources.title: Illinois Secretary of State, Driver's License and State ID FAQ
sources.said: An Illinois driver's license is valid for 4 years. An Illinois ID card is valid for 5 years.

sources.title: Illinois Secretary of State, Driver's License and State ID Card Information
sources.said: If you are under 21, please review the Graduated Driver's License page. ... Drivers ages 21 through 86 — licenses are valid for 4 years and expire on the driver's birthday ... Drivers age 87 and older must renew their licenses each year ... Residents over age 65: Visit a DMV to apply for a free non-expiring state ID card.
